headline: Microsoft cuts 4,800 jobs as AI drives tech layoffs in 2026
summary: Microsoft eliminated 2.1% of its global workforce, citing AI's impact on work. This adds to the over 120,000 tech roles cut this year.
details: Microsoft announced on Monday that it has laid off approximately 4,800 employees, representing 2.1% of its global workforce. The company stated that these roles are not being replaced by AI, but acknowledged that AI is transforming how work is done and automating tasks.

This move by Microsoft contributes to a growing trend of AI-related layoffs across the tech industry. Companies are reporting record revenues while simultaneously reducing staff, often citing AI as both a driver of growth and a reason for workforce reductions.

According to outplacement firm Challenger, Gray & Christmas, May saw the highest number of tech layoffs in years, with AI being the most frequently cited reason. Layoffs.fyi reports that over 120,000 tech jobs have been eliminated in 2026.

Other major tech companies have also announced significant layoffs this year, with AI as a stated factor. Oracle cut 21,000 employees, citing AI adoption. GitLab reduced its staff by 350 to fund AI infrastructure and handle increased AI workflow traffic.

Google has been cutting employees across its Cloud division, with estimates ranging from 1,500 to 3,000+ engineers. Intuit plans to eliminate about 3,000 jobs, reallocating resources toward AI. Meta laid off 8,000 employees while moving 7,000 into new AI roles.

Cisco is cutting nearly 4,000 jobs, realigning resources around AI, silicon, optics, and security. Cloudflare reduced its workforce by 1,100, with many of the cuts in middle management and support roles, despite reporting record revenue.
